key_insight: Turning code optimization into a reinforcement learning reward is much harder than code correctness. In practice, timing noise, sparse rewards, and RL instability can outweigh the performance signal, so models get only marginally faster and can become less correct.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of using reinforcement learning to optimize code execution time, rather than just code correctness, in a setting where runtime is noisy and improvements are subtle.
method: Frame code optimization as an RL problem where reward depends on execution time, alongside correctness.
Investigate how timing noise, reward sparsity, and GRPO instability affect training dynamics.
Analyze why standard RL setups that work for correctness fail to reliably improve code speed.
impact: This matters because it shows that naive reward design is not enough for performance optimization tasks. Practitioners working on code generation or RL-based optimization need more robust signals, better measurement strategies, or alternative training methods.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: code generation → execution → timing measurement → reward signal
Comparison chart showing correctness-based RL vs timing-based RL outcomes
Noise/instability illustration highlighting small speed gains versus increased failures
Icon set for runtime, hidden tests, reward, and warning/stability
paper_authors: Pierre Chambon, Kunhao Zheng, Juliette Decugis, Benoit Sagot, Gabriel Synnaeve
